findings.source: Stapmanns et al. 2021, Frontiers in Neuroinformatics 15:609147, DOI 10.3389/fninf.2021.609147
findings.finding: Plasticity rules that depend continuously on postsynaptic membrane-potential history do not inherently require time-driven or all-synapse updates. Two history-archiving algorithms are compatible with event-based synapse updates and significantly outperform time-driven updates for Clopath and Urbanczik-Senn rules in the reported regimes.
findings.impact: Continuous hidden/plasticity state or delayed credit history is not sufficient justification for global eligibility traversal; equal-semantics event-driven archival is established ordinary prior art.

findings.source: Stapmanns et al. 2021, Frontiers in Neuroinformatics 15:609147, DOI 10.3389/fninf.2021.609147
findings.finding: Event-driven schemes trade fewer synapse function calls for stored history and history-management work; compressed variants add dependence on in-degree, spike-time diversity and heterogeneous delays.
findings.impact: Operation-count reduction alone is not a universal efficiency result; prospective claims should bind memory/history cost and workload crossover variables.

findings.finding: EventProp computes exact gradients for its continuous-time spiking model by propagating errors at spike times and storing state only at spike times rather than on a dense time grid.
findings.impact: Exactness or continuous-time semantics do not by themselves justify dense bookkeeping; an optimized equal-semantics comparator may remain event-sparse.

findings.finding: Stable SparkBrain decays eligibility across every connection before every processed event and reward application scans all connections. The strongest prospective comparator is therefore timestamp/history-lazy state reconstruction with exact trajectory checks plus explicit history/timestamp/memory accounting.
findings.impact: The active R48 object remains SYSTEM resource characterization; a positive local-work result should be bounded to the measured resource vector and workload regime, not treated as mechanism novelty or universal efficiency.

novelty_or_reduction_impact: CONTINUOUS_STATE_EVENT_DRIVEN_REDUCTION_AND_RESOURCE_CROSSOVER_SHARPENING_NO_MECHANISM_NOVELTY_UPLIFT. Event-driven plasticity remains feasible even when learning depends on continuous postsynaptic state history, and exact continuous-time gradients can be event-sparse. Fair comparison must therefore include equal-semantics state archiving/lazy materialization and account for memory/history overhead and crossover regime, not only operation counts.
prospective_baselines_or_discriminators: current global eligibility traversal versus event-triggered/timestamp-lazy eligibility that reconstructs exactly the state needed at access/update time
continuous-state event-driven history-archive comparator preserving the same postsynaptic/plasticity information
